chapters.title: My God, My God
chapters.html:
Psalms 22

For the director: on "The Doe of the Dawn." A psalm of David.

Why Have You Forsaken Me?

1My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?
Far from my salvation are the words of my groaning.

2My God, I cry by day, and You do not answer,
and by night, and there is no rest for me.

3Yet You are holy,
enthroned on the praises of Israel.

4In You our fathers trusted;
they trusted, and You rescued them.

5To You they cried out and were delivered;
in You they trusted and were not put to shame.

6But I am a worm and not a man,
scorned by men and despised by the people.

7All who see me mock me;
they make mouths at me; they shake their heads:

8"He committed himself to the LORD; let Him rescue him;
let Him deliver him, for He delights in him!"

9Yet You are the one who drew me from the womb;
You made me trust at my mother's breasts.

10On You I was cast from birth;
from my mother's womb You have been my God.

11Do not be far from me,
for trouble is near,
and there is no one to help.

Like Water Poured Out

12Many bulls surround me;
strong bulls of Bashan encircle me;

13they open their mouths wide at me,
like a lion tearing and roaring.

14I am poured out like water,
and all my bones are out of joint;
my heart has become like wax;
it is melted within me.

15My strength is dried up like a piece of pottery,
and my tongue clings to my jaws;
You lay me in the dust of death.

16For dogs surround me;
a company of evildoers encircles me;
they have pierced my hands and my feet.

17I can count all my bones;
they look and stare at me;

18they divide my garments among them,
and for my clothing they cast lots.

19But You, LORD, do not be far away;
my strength, hurry to help me.

20Rescue my soul from the sword,
my only life from the power of the dog.

21Save me from the mouth of the lion;
from the horns of the wild oxen You have answered me.

In the Great Congregation

22I will tell of Your name to my brothers;
among the congregation I will praise You.

23You who fear the LORD, praise Him;
all you descendants of Jacob, glorify Him;
stand in awe of Him, all you descendants of Israel.

24For He has not despised or loathed the affliction of the afflicted,
nor hidden His face from him,
but heard when he cried to Him.

25From You comes my praise in the great congregation;
I will pay my vows before those who fear Him.

26The humble will eat and be satisfied;
those who seek Him will praise the LORD.
May your hearts live forever!

27All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the LORD,
and all the families of the nations will bow down before You.

28For the kingdom belongs to the LORD,
and He rules over the nations.

29All the prosperous of the earth will eat and bow down;
before Him will kneel all who go down to the dust,
and the one who cannot keep his soul alive.

30Offspring will serve Him;
it will be told of the Lord to the generation to come.

31They will come and declare His righteousness
to a people yet to be born, that He has done it.

Notes

  • The title "on 'The Doe of the Dawn'" — al ayyelet ha-shachar, the name of a tune.

  • v1 "My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?" — Eli Eli lamah azavtani. Jesus cried these words from the cross in Aramaic, Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani (Mark 15:34; Matthew 27:46). The psalm moves from abandonment (vv1–21) to praise (vv22–31).

  • v1 "the words of my groaning" — sha'agati, my roaring, the cry of a lion or of a man in agony (32:3; Job 3:24).

  • v8 "He committed himself to the LORD; let Him rescue him" — the words the mockers spoke at the cross (Matthew 27:43). Committed is gol, roll (your way) onto the LORD (37:5).

  • v12 "strong bulls of Bashan" — the rich cattle land east of the Jordan (Amos 4:1; Deuteronomy 32:14).

  • v16 "they have pierced my hands and my feet" — the Leningrad text has ka'ari, like a lion, like a lion my hands and my feet, a line with no verb. The Greek, the Syriac and the Latin read they have pierced (or dug), and one of the oldest Hebrew copies, found near the Dead Sea, has ka'aru, a verb; the reading of the witnesses is followed here (witness rule 2).

  • v18 "they divide my garments among them" — fulfilled at the cross, as John says in quoting the line (John 19:23–24; Mark 15:24).

  • v22 "I will tell of Your name to my brothers" — quoted in Hebrews 2:12 as the words of Jesus. The turn from lament to praise is sudden: You have answered me (v21).

  • v24 "despised or loathed" — shiqqets, loathe, as the word table has it.

  • vv27–31 — the praise widens to all the ends of the earth, to the dead (v29) and to those not yet born (v31). He has done it is the psalm's last word.

speech.text: Psalms 22
Why Have You Forsaken Me?
My God, my God, why have You forsaken me? Far from my salvation are the words of my groaning.
My God, I cry by day, and You do not answer, and by night, and there is no rest for me.
Yet You are holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel.
In You our fathers trusted; they trusted, and You rescued them.
To You they cried out and were delivered; in You they trusted and were not put to shame.
But I am a worm and not a man, scorned by men and despised by the people.
All who see me mock me; they make mouths at me; they shake their heads:
"He committed himself to the LORD; let Him rescue him; let Him deliver him, for He delights in him!"
Yet You are the one who drew me from the womb; You made me trust at my mother's breasts.
On You I was cast from birth; from my mother's womb You have been my God.
Do not be far from me, for trouble is near, and there is no one to help.
Like Water Poured Out
Many bulls surround me; strong bulls of Bashan encircle me;
they open their mouths wide at me, like a lion tearing and roaring.
I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint; my heart has become like wax; it is melted within me.
My strength is dried up like a piece of pottery, and my tongue clings to my jaws; You lay me in the dust of death.
For dogs surround me; a company of evildoers encircles me; they have pierced my hands and my feet.
I can count all my bones; they look and stare at me;
they divide my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots.
But You, LORD, do not be far away; my strength, hurry to help me.
Rescue my soul from the sword, my only life from the power of the dog.
Save me from the mouth of the lion; from the horns of the wild oxen You have answered me.
In the Great Congregation
I will tell of Your name to my brothers; among the congregation I will praise You.
You who fear the LORD, praise Him; all you descendants of Jacob, glorify Him; stand in awe of Him, all you descendants of Israel.
For He has not despised or loathed the affliction of the afflicted, nor hidden His face from him, but heard when he cried to Him.
From You comes my praise in the great congregation; I will pay my vows before those who fear Him.
The humble will eat and be satisfied; those who seek Him will praise the LORD. May your hearts live forever!
All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the LORD, and all the families of the nations will bow down before You.
For the kingdom belongs to the LORD, and He rules over the nations.
All the prosperous of the earth will eat and bow down; before Him will kneel all who go down to the dust, and the one who cannot keep his soul alive.
Offspring will serve Him; it will be told of the Lord to the generation to come.
They will come and declare His righteousness to a people yet to be born, that He has done it.

chapters.title: The LORD Is My Shepherd
chapters.html:
Psalms 23

A psalm of David.

1The LORD is my shepherd; I lack nothing.

2He makes me lie down in green pastures;
He leads me beside still waters.

3He brings back my soul;
He guides me in paths of righteousness
for His name's sake.

4Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death,
I fear no evil, for You are with me;
Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.

5You prepare a table before me
in the presence of my enemies;
You anoint my head with oil;
my cup overflows.

6Surely goodness and loyal love will pursue me
all the days of my life,
and I will dwell in the house of the LORD
for length of days.

Notes

  • v1 "The LORD is my shepherd" — YHWH ro'i: the king as shepherd of his people (2 Samuel 5:2), and God as Israel's shepherd (80:1; Genesis 48:15; Ezekiel 34:11–16). David was a shepherd before he was a king (1 Samuel 16:11). I am the good shepherd (John 10:11).

  • v2 "still waters" — mei menuchot, waters of rest, the quiet water a flock can drink from safely.

  • v3 "He brings back my soul" — yeshovev, restores life, as in 19:7; or brings back the strayed sheep. Paths of righteousness are the right tracks, and also the ways of right living.

  • v4 "the valley of the shadow of death" — gei tsalmavet, a valley of deep darkness (Job 10:21–22; Jeremiah 2:6). Rod and staff: the club against beasts and the crook to guide.

  • v4 "for You are with me" — at the center of the psalm the speech turns from He to You.

  • v5 "You prepare a table before me" — the shepherd becomes a host; a host who anoints his guest's head with oil (Luke 7:46) and keeps his cup full, while the enemies look on and cannot touch him.

  • v6 "goodness and loyal love will pursue me" — yirdefuni, the word for enemies in pursuit (7:1): instead of foes, God's goodness and chesed are at his heels.

  • v6 "I will dwell in the house of the LORD" — the Hebrew has ve-shavti, and I will return; the Greek and most translations read ve-yashavti, and I will dwell, as in 27:4, followed here. For length of days, le-orekh yamim, is for all one's life, and beyond.

speech.text: Psalms 23
The LORD is my shepherd; I lack nothing.
He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside still waters.
He brings back my soul; He guides me in paths of righteousness for His name's sake.
Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.
You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.
Surely goodness and loyal love will pursue me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for length of days.

chapters.title: The King of Glory
chapters.html:
Psalms 24

Of David. A psalm.

1The earth is the LORD's, and all that fills it,
the world and those who live in it,

2for He has founded it on the seas
and established it on the rivers.

3Who shall go up the mountain of the LORD?
Who shall stand in His holy place?

4The one who has clean hands and a pure heart,
who has not lifted up his soul to what is false
and has not sworn deceitfully.

5He will receive a blessing from the LORD
and righteousness from the God of his salvation.

6Such is the generation of those who seek Him,
who seek Your face, God of Jacob. Selah

7Lift up your heads, you gates,
and be lifted up, you everlasting doors,
that the King of glory may come in.

8Who is this King of glory?
The LORD, strong and mighty,
the LORD, mighty in battle.

9Lift up your heads, you gates,
and lift them up, you everlasting doors,
that the King of glory may come in.

10Who is He, this King of glory?
The LORD of hosts,
He is the King of glory. Selah

Notes

  • v1 "The earth is the LORD's, and all that fills it" — quoted by Paul of food offered to idols: everything is the Lord's (1 Corinthians 10:26; Exodus 19:5).

  • v2 "founded it on the seas" — the earth set firm above the waters of the deep (136:6; Genesis 1:9–10).

  • vv3–6 — a gate liturgy like Psalm 15: the question at the entrance of the temple and the answer.

  • v4 "who has not lifted up his soul to what is false" — the written text has nafsho, his soul, followed here; the read form has nafshi, My soul, God's own life, as in you shall not take up the name of the LORD your God in vain (Exodus 20:7).

  • v6 "God of Jacob" — the Hebrew has only Jacob: who seek Your face, Jacob; the Greek and Syriac read the face of the God of Jacob, followed here, since Jacob is not the one being sought.

  • vv7–10 "Lift up your heads, you gates" — the ark of the LORD coming up into Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6:12–15), the gates told to grow tall for the King who enters. The Church has sung the verses of Christ's ascension.

  • v8 "mighty in battle" — The LORD is a man of war (Exodus 15:3). The ark went before Israel in battle (Numbers 10:35).

  • v10 "The LORD of hosts" — YHWH tseva'ot, the LORD of the armies of heaven and of Israel (1 Samuel 17:45), the answer to the question asked twice.

chapters.title: To You, LORD, I Lift Up My Soul
chapters.html:
Psalms 25

Of David.

1To You, LORD, I lift up my soul.

2My God, in You I trust;
let me not be put to shame;
let not my enemies exult over me.

3Indeed, none who wait for You will be put to shame;
those who are treacherous without cause will be put to shame.

4Make Your ways known to me, LORD;
teach me Your paths.

5Lead me in Your truth and teach me,
for You are the God of my salvation;
for You I wait all the day.

6Remember Your compassion, LORD, and Your loyal love,
for they have been from of old.

7Do not remember the sins of my youth or my transgressions;
according to Your loyal love remember me,
for the sake of Your goodness, LORD.

8Good and upright is the LORD;
therefore He instructs sinners in the way.

9He leads the humble in what is right
and teaches the humble His way.

10All the paths of the LORD are loyal love and faithfulness
for those who keep His covenant and His testimonies.

11For Your name's sake, LORD,
pardon my iniquity, for it is great.

12Who is the man who fears the LORD?
He will instruct him in the way he should choose.

13His soul will lodge in good things,
and his offspring will inherit the land.

14The friendship of the LORD is for those who fear Him,
and He makes His covenant known to them.

15My eyes are always toward the LORD,
for He will bring my feet out of the net.

16Turn to me and be gracious to me,
for I am alone and afflicted.

17The troubles of my heart have grown wide;
bring me out of my distress.

18See my affliction and my trouble,
and forgive all my sins.

19See how many are my enemies,
and with what violent hatred they hate me.

20Guard my soul and rescue me;
let me not be put to shame, for I take refuge in You.

21Let integrity and uprightness keep me,
for I wait for You.

22Redeem Israel, God,
out of all his troubles.

Notes

  • The psalm — an acrostic: each verse begins with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet, with a few letters missing or doubled. The last verse stands outside the alphabet, a prayer for all Israel; Psalm 34 ends the same way.

  • v1 "To You, LORD, I lift up my soul" — nafshi essa, to long for, to set one's desire on (86:4; 143:8).

  • v3 "those who wait for You" — qoveikha, from qavah, wait, hope, the root of tiqvah, hope (Job 7:6); the word returns in vv5 and 21.

  • v7 "the sins of my youth" — sins done without understanding (Job 13:26). Remember me according to chesed, not according to sin.

  • v8 "He instructs sinners in the way" — yoreh, the root of torah: God teaches even sinners, because He is good.

  • v13 "his offspring will inherit the land" — the meek shall inherit the land (37:11; Matthew 5:5).

  • v14 "The friendship of the LORD" — sod YHWH, God's close counsel, as Job had it once (Job 29:4).

  • v17 "The troubles of my heart have grown wide" — or, with the words divided differently, relieve the troubles of my heart, the reverse of distress (4:1).

  • v21 "integrity and uprightness" — tom va-yosher, the words used of Job (Job 1:1), here as guards set to keep the psalmist.

chapters.title: I Have Walked in My Integrity
chapters.html:
Psalms 26

Of David.

1Vindicate me, LORD,
for I have walked in my integrity,
and I have trusted in the LORD without wavering.

2Test me, LORD, and try me;
refine my mind and my heart.

3For Your loyal love is before my eyes,
and I walk in Your faithfulness.

4I do not sit with men of falsehood,
nor do I go in with those who hide what they are.

5I hate the assembly of evildoers,
and I will not sit with the wicked.

6I wash my hands in innocence
and go around Your altar, LORD,

7to make the sound of thanksgiving heard
and tell of all Your wonders.

8LORD, I love the dwelling of Your house
and the place where Your glory lives.

9Do not gather my soul away with sinners,
nor my life with men of bloodshed,

10in whose hands are evil schemes,
and whose right hand is full of bribes.

11But as for me, I walk in my integrity;
redeem me, and be gracious to me.

12My foot stands on level ground;
in the assemblies I will bless the LORD.

Notes

  • v1 "Vindicate me, LORD" — shofteni, judge me: the plea of an innocent man who asks for a verdict, as in 7:8 and 17:1–3.

  • v1 "my integrity" — tummi, the word of Job 2:3 and 27:5; it frames the psalm (v11).

  • v2 "my mind and my heart" — kilyotai ve-libbi, my kidneys and my heart (7:9; 16:7). Refine is the read form tsorfah; the written form has the same letters in another order.

  • v4 "those who hide what they are" — na'alamim, the concealed, hypocrites.

  • v6 "I wash my hands in innocence" — a sign of innocence before God (73:13; Deuteronomy 21:6–7), before going to the altar. Go around Your altar is the procession of worshipers (118:27).

  • v8 "the place where Your glory lives" — mishkan kevodekha, the dwelling of the glory that filled the tabernacle (Exodus 40:34–35).

  • v9 "Do not gather my soul away with sinners" — al te'esof, as death gathers a man to his people: let me not die the death of the wicked.

  • v12 "level ground" — mishor, a place where the foot cannot slip (27:11); the assemblies are the gatherings of worshipers.

For Your loyal love is before my eyes, and I walk in Your faithfulness.
I do not sit with men of falsehood, nor do I go in with those who hide what they are.
I hate the assembly of evildoers, and I will not sit with the wicked.

chapters.title: The LORD Is My Light
chapters.html:
Psalms 27

Of David.

1The LORD is my light and my salvation;
whom shall I fear?
The LORD is the stronghold of my life;
of whom shall I be afraid?

2When evildoers came near me
to eat up my flesh,
my adversaries and my enemies,
they stumbled and fell.

3Though an army camp against me,
my heart will not fear;
though war rise against me,
even then I will be confident.

4One thing I have asked of the LORD;
that I will seek:
to dwell in the house of the LORD
all the days of my life,
to gaze on the beauty of the LORD
and to inquire in His temple.

5For He will hide me in His shelter
in the day of trouble;
He will conceal me in the hiding place of His tent;
He will lift me high on a rock.

6Now my head will be lifted up
above my enemies around me,
and I will offer in His tent
sacrifices with shouts of joy;
I will sing and make music to the LORD.

7Hear, LORD, my voice when I call;
be gracious to me and answer me.

8My heart says of You, "Seek My face."
Your face, LORD, I will seek.

9Do not hide Your face from me;
do not turn Your servant away in anger;
You have been my help.
Do not cast me off or forsake me,
God of my salvation.

10For my father and my mother have forsaken me,
but the LORD will take me in.

11Teach me Your way, LORD,
and lead me on a level path
because of those who watch me.

12Do not give me up to the will of my adversaries,
for false witnesses have risen against me,
and they breathe out violence.

13If I had not believed that I would see the goodness of the LORD
in the land of the living —

14Wait for the LORD;
be strong, and let your heart take courage;
wait for the LORD!

Notes

  • v1 "The LORD is my light" — ori; when I sit in darkness, the LORD will be a light to me (Micah 7:8); the LORD will be your everlasting light (Isaiah 60:19–20; John 8:12).

  • v2 "to eat up my flesh" — enemies as wild beasts (14:4; Daniel 7:5).

  • v4 "One thing I have asked of the LORD" — the center of the psalm: not deliverance only, but to live in God's presence (23:6). To inquire, le-vaqqer, is to seek guidance, or to look with delight.

  • v5 "He will hide me in His shelter" — sukko, His booth, His tent: the hospitality of the host who must protect his guest (15:1; 61:4).

  • v8 "My heart says of You, 'Seek My face'" — the Hebrew is compressed, To You my heart has said, Seek My face: the heart repeats God's own invitation and answers it.

  • v10 "For my father and my mother have forsaken me" — or even if they forsake me; take me in, ya'asfeni, as a stray is gathered into a household.

  • v13 "If I had not believed" — lule, marked in the Hebrew text with special dots above and below, the scribes' sign of a doubtful word; the Greek lacks it, and reads I believe that I will see. With the word, the sentence breaks off: If I had not believed… (I would have perished).

  • v13 "the land of the living" — this life, as against Sheol (116:9; Isaiah 38:11).

  • v14 "Wait for the LORD" — qavveh, the hope of 25:3; the psalm ends speaking to the soul, or to every hearer.

The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
When evildoers came near me to eat up my flesh, my adversaries and my enemies, they stumbled and fell.
Though an army camp against me, my heart will not fear; though war rise against me, even then I will be confident.
One thing I have asked of the LORD; that I will seek: to dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to gaze on the beauty of the LORD and to inquire in His temple.
For He will hide me in His shelter in the day of trouble; He will conceal me in the hiding place of His tent; He will lift me high on a rock.
Now my head will be lifted up above my enemies around me, and I will offer in His tent sacrifices with shouts of joy; I will sing and make music to the LORD.
Hear, LORD, my voice when I call; be gracious to me and answer me.
My heart says of You, "Seek My face." Your face, LORD, I will seek.
Do not hide Your face from me; do not turn Your servant away in anger; You have been my help. Do not cast me off or forsake me, God of my salvation.
For my father and my mother have forsaken me, but the LORD will take me in.
Teach me Your way, LORD, and lead me on a level path because of those who watch me.
Do not give me up to the will of my adversaries, for false witnesses have risen against me, and they breathe out violence.
If I had not believed that I would see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living —
Wait for the LORD; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait for the LORD!

chapters.title: The LORD Is My Strength and My Shield
chapters.html:
Psalms 28

Of David.

1To You, LORD, I call;
my rock, do not be deaf to me,
or, if You are silent to me,
I will become like those who go down to the pit.

2Hear the sound of my pleas for mercy
when I cry to You for help,
when I lift up my hands
toward Your holy inner sanctuary.

3Do not drag me away with the wicked,
with those who do iniquity,
who speak peace with their neighbors
while evil is in their hearts.

4Give to them according to their work
and according to the evil of their deeds;
give to them according to the work of their hands;
pay them back what they deserve.

5Because they do not consider the deeds of the LORD
or the work of His hands,
He will tear them down and not build them up.

6Blessed be the LORD,
for He has heard the sound of my pleas for mercy.

7The LORD is my strength and my shield;
in Him my heart trusts, and I am helped;
my heart exults,
and with my song I give thanks to Him.

8The LORD is their strength;
He is the saving stronghold of His anointed.

9Save Your people and bless Your inheritance;
shepherd them and carry them forever.

Notes

  • v1 "do not be deaf to me" — al techerash, the silence of God is the psalmist's fear; the pit, bor, is the grave (30:3; 88:4).

  • v2 "Your holy inner sanctuary" — devir, the innermost room of the temple, where the ark stood (1 Kings 6:5, 19–23). Prayer was made with lifted hands toward it (1 Kings 8:29–30; 1 Timothy 2:8).

  • v3 "who speak peace with their neighbors while evil is in their hearts" — the double heart of 12:2; with his mouth each speaks peace to his neighbor, but in his heart he plans an ambush (Jeremiah 9:8).

  • v4 "pay them back what they deserve" — the plea that God's justice match the deed (62:12; Revelation 22:12).

  • v5 "He will tear them down and not build them up" — the words of Jeremiah's call, to break down… to build (Jeremiah 1:10; 24:6).

  • v6 "Blessed be the LORD, for He has heard" — the turn from plea to thanks comes in the middle of the psalm, as in 6:8–9 and 22:21.

  • v8 "The LORD is their strength" — oz lamo, strength to them, His people; the Greek, Syriac and some Hebrew manuscripts read le-ammo, the strength of His people. His anointed is the king (2:2; 20:6).

  • v9 "shepherd them and carry them forever" — the LORD as shepherd (23:1), who carries His lambs in His arms (Isaiah 40:11; Deuteronomy 1:31).

speech.text: Psalms 28
To You, LORD, I call; my rock, do not be deaf to me, or, if You are silent to me, I will become like those who go down to the pit.
Hear the sound of my pleas for mercy when I cry to You for help, when I lift up my hands toward Your holy inner sanctuary.
Do not drag me away with the wicked, with those who do iniquity, who speak peace with their neighbors while evil is in their hearts.
Give to them according to their work and according to the evil of their deeds; give to them according to the work of their hands; pay them back what they deserve.
Because they do not consider the deeds of the LORD or the work of His hands, He will tear them down and not build them up.
Blessed be the LORD, for He has heard the sound of my pleas for mercy.
The LORD is my strength and my shield; in Him my heart trusts, and I am helped; my heart exults, and with my song I give thanks to Him.
The LORD is their strength; He is the saving stronghold of His anointed.
Save Your people and bless Your inheritance; shepherd them and carry them forever.

chapters.title: The Voice of the LORD
chapters.html:
Psalms 29

A psalm of David.

1Ascribe to the LORD, you sons of God,
ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.

2Ascribe to the LORD the glory of His name;
bow down to the LORD in the splendor of holiness.

3The voice of the LORD is over the waters;
the God of glory thunders,
the LORD, over many waters.

4The voice of the LORD is in power;
the voice of the LORD is in majesty.

5The voice of the LORD breaks the cedars;
the LORD breaks the cedars of Lebanon.

6He makes them skip like a calf,
Lebanon and Sirion like a young wild ox.

7The voice of the LORD strikes out flames of fire.

8The voice of the LORD shakes the wilderness;
the LORD shakes the wilderness of Kadesh.

9The voice of the LORD makes the deer give birth
and strips the forests bare,
and in His temple all say, "Glory!"

10The LORD sat enthroned over the flood;
the LORD sits enthroned as King forever.

11The LORD will give strength to His people;
the LORD will bless His people with peace.

Notes

  • v1 "you sons of God" — benei elim, the heavenly beings of God's court (89:6; Job 1:6), called to praise Him before the storm is described.

  • v2 "in the splendor of holiness" — be-hadrat qodesh, the beauty of holiness, or the holy attire of worshipers (96:9; 1 Chronicles 16:29).

  • vv3–9 "The voice of the LORD" — qol YHWH, seven times, the seven peals of the thunderstorm. The storm rolls in from the Mediterranean (many waters), over the mountains of the north (Lebanon and Sirion), and into the southern wilderness (Kadesh).

  • v6 "Sirion" — the Sidonian name for Mount Hermon (Deuteronomy 3:9). A young wild ox, ben re'emim (Job 39:9).

  • v7 "strikes out flames of fire" — chotsev, hews, as stone is cut: the lightning splits the air.

  • v9 "makes the deer give birth" — yecholel ayyalot; read with other vowels, eilot, oaks: makes the oaks whirl, which suits strips the forests bare in the next line.

  • v9 "in His temple all say, 'Glory!'" — the heavenly temple, answering the call of vv1–2.

  • v10 "The LORD sat enthroned over the flood" — mabbul, a word used elsewhere only of Noah's flood (Genesis 6–11): as He ruled over that flood, so He rules over every storm.

  • v11 "the LORD will bless His people with peace" — the last word of the psalm is shalom, after the storm.

The voice of the LORD is in power; the voice of the LORD is in majesty.

chapters.title: Joy Comes in the Morning
chapters.html:
Psalms 30

A psalm. A song at the dedication of the house. Of David.

1I will exalt You, LORD, for You have drawn me up
and have not let my enemies rejoice over me.

2LORD my God, I cried to You for help,
and You healed me.

3LORD, You brought up my soul from Sheol;
You kept me alive, so that I did not go down to the pit.

4Sing praise to the LORD, you His faithful ones,
and give thanks to the remembrance of His holiness.

5For His anger is for a moment,
His favor for a lifetime.
Weeping may lodge for the evening,
but at morning there is a shout of joy.

6As for me, I said in my ease,
"I will never be moved."

7LORD, by Your favor
You had set my mountain firm;
You hid Your face; I was dismayed.

8To You, LORD, I called,
and to the Lord I pleaded for mercy:

9"What profit is there in my blood,
if I go down to the pit?
Will the dust praise You?
Will it tell of Your faithfulness?

10Hear, LORD, and be gracious to me;
LORD, be my helper."

11You have turned my mourning into dancing for me;
You have loosed my sackcloth
and clothed me with gladness,

12so that my glory may sing praise to You and not be silent.
LORD my God, I will give thanks to You forever.

Notes

  • The title "A song at the dedication of the house" — chanukkat ha-bayit: perhaps David's own house (2 Samuel 5:11), or the site of the temple (1 Chronicles 22:1); later sung at the rededication of the temple, the feast of Hanukkah.

  • v1 "You have drawn me up" — dillitani, as a bucket is drawn up from a well.

  • v3 "You kept me alive, so that I did not go down to the pit" — the read form, mi-yordi, from my going down; the written form has mi-yordei, from among those who go down.

  • v4 "the remembrance of His holiness" — zekher qodsho, His holy name, by which He is remembered (Exodus 3:15; 97:12).

  • v5 "Weeping may lodge for the evening" — yalin, spend the night, like a guest who leaves in the morning.

  • vv6–7 "I said in my ease, 'I will never be moved'" — the words of the wicked in 10:6, spoken by the psalmist in his prosperity; God hid His face, and he learned better.

  • vv9–10 — the prayer he prayed in his trouble, quoted: the dead do not praise God (6:5; 88:10–12).

  • v11 "You have turned my mourning into dancing" — you will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will turn into joy (John 16:20; Jeremiah 31:13).

  • v12 "my glory" — kavod, the self, the soul, as in 16:9.

chapters.title: Into Your Hand I Commit My Spirit
chapters.html:
Psalms 31

For the director. A psalm of David.

1In You, LORD, I take refuge;
let me never be put to shame;
in Your righteousness rescue me.

2Incline Your ear to me;
deliver me quickly;
be a rock of refuge for me,
a strong fortress to save me.

3For You are my rock and my fortress;
for Your name's sake You lead me and guide me.

4You bring me out of the net they have hidden for me,
for You are my refuge.

5Into Your hand I commit my spirit;
You have redeemed me, LORD, God of truth.

6I hate those who hold to empty idols,
but I trust in the LORD.

7I will rejoice and be glad in Your loyal love,
because You have seen my affliction;
You have known the distress of my soul,

8and You have not handed me over to the enemy;
You have set my feet in a broad place.

9Be gracious to me, LORD, for I am in distress;
my eye wastes away with grief,
my soul and my body also.

10For my life is spent with sorrow,
and my years with sighing;
my strength stumbles because of my iniquity,
and my bones waste away.

11Because of all my adversaries I have become a reproach,
above all to my neighbors,
and a dread to those who know me;
those who see me in the street flee from me.

12I am forgotten like the dead, out of mind;
I have become like a broken vessel.

13For I hear the whispering of many,
terror on every side,
as they plot together against me,
as they scheme to take my life.

14But I trust in You, LORD;
I say, "You are my God."

15My times are in Your hand;
rescue me from the hand of my enemies and from those who pursue me.

16Make Your face shine on Your servant;
save me in Your loyal love.

17LORD, let me not be put to shame, for I call on You;
let the wicked be put to shame;
let them be silent in Sheol.

18Let the lying lips be mute,
which speak arrogantly against the righteous
in pride and contempt.

19How great is Your goodness,
which You have stored up for those who fear You
and worked for those who take refuge in You
in the sight of the children of man!

20In the shelter of Your presence You hide them
from the plots of men;
You keep them safe in Your shelter
from the strife of tongues.

21Blessed be the LORD,
for He has shown me the wonder of His loyal love
in a city under siege.

22As for me, I said in my alarm,
"I am cut off from before Your eyes."
But You heard the sound of my pleas for mercy
when I cried to You for help.

23Love the LORD, all you His faithful ones!
The LORD keeps the faithful
and repays in full the one who acts in pride.

24Be strong, and let your heart take courage,
all you who wait for the LORD!

Notes

  • vv1–3 — the same words open Psalm 71 (71:1–3).

  • v5 "Into Your hand I commit my spirit" — ruchi, the psalmist's own spirit, his life, placed in God's keeping. Jesus prayed these words on the cross, adding Father (Luke 23:46); Stephen prayed them to Jesus (Acts 7:59).

  • v6 "I hate those who hold to empty idols" — havlei shav, vapors of emptiness, idols (Jonah 2:8). The Greek and Syriac read You hate.

  • v10 "because of my iniquity" — ba-avoni; the Greek and Syriac read be-onyi, because of my affliction.

  • v12 "like a broken vessel" — a pot that is thrown away (Jeremiah 22:28; 48:38).

  • v13 "terror on every side" — magor missaviv, Jeremiah's watchword, and the name his enemies gave him (Jeremiah 6:25; 20:3–4, 10).

  • v15 "My times are in Your hand" — the times of a man's life, its seasons and its end (1 Chronicles 29:30), held by God, not by his enemies.

  • v16 "Make Your face shine on Your servant" — the priestly blessing again (4:6; Numbers 6:25).

  • v21 "in a city under siege" — be-ir matsor, or a fortified city: God's loyal love itself is the stronghold.

  • v22 "I am cut off from before Your eyes" — nigrazti, as Jonah said, I am driven away from Your sight (Jonah 2:4).

chapters.title: Blessed Is the One Whose Transgression Is Forgiven
chapters.html:
Psalms 32

Of David. A Maskil.

1Blessed is the one whose transgression is forgiven,
whose sin is covered.

2Blessed is the man to whom the LORD counts no iniquity,
and in whose spirit there is no deceit.

3When I kept silent, my bones wasted away
through my groaning all day long.

4For day and night Your hand was heavy on me;
my strength was dried up as by the heat of summer. Selah

5I made my sin known to You,
and I did not cover my iniquity;
I said, "I will confess my transgressions to the LORD,"
and You forgave the iniquity of my sin. Selah

6Therefore let everyone who is faithful pray to You
at a time when You may be found;
surely in the rush of great waters
they will not reach him.

7You are a hiding place for me;
You keep me from trouble;
You surround me with shouts of deliverance. Selah

8I will instruct you and teach you in the way you should go;
I will counsel you with My eye on you.

9Do not be like a horse or a mule, without understanding,
whose trappings must be bit and bridle to hold it in,
or it will not come near you.

10Many are the sorrows of the wicked,
but loyal love surrounds the one who trusts in the LORD.

11Be glad in the LORD and rejoice, you righteous;
shout for joy, all you upright in heart!

Notes

  • The title "A Maskil" — maskil, from haskil, to give insight, the heading of thirteen psalms; perhaps a teaching song, or a skilled one. The word returns in v8, askilkha, I will instruct you.

  • The psalm — the second of the seven penitential psalms (see 6).

  • vv1–2 "Blessed is the one whose transgression is forgiven" — three words for sin (pesha, transgression; chata'ah, sin; avon, iniquity) and three for forgiveness (forgiven, nesui, lifted away; covered; not counted). Paul quotes the verses of righteousness counted apart from works (Romans 4:6–8).

  • v3 "When I kept silent" — silence about his sin, not silence before men; the groaning was the body's protest.

  • v4 "my strength was dried up" — leshaddi, a word found only here and in Numbers 11:8, perhaps my vitality, my sap.

  • v5 "I will confess my transgressions to the LORD" — If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us (1 John 1:9; Proverbs 28:13).

  • v6 "at a time when You may be found" — Seek the LORD while He may be found (Isaiah 55:6). The rush of great waters is the flood of judgment.

  • v8 "I will instruct you… with My eye on you" — God now speaks; His pronouns are capitalized. Some take the speaker to be the psalmist teaching others, as in 51:13.

  • v9 "like a horse or a mule" — animals that must be led by force; the forgiven are led by God's eye.

chapters.title: Sing to Him a New Song
chapters.html:
Psalms 33

1Shout for joy in the LORD, you righteous;
praise is fitting for the upright.

2Give thanks to the LORD with the lyre;
make music to Him with the ten-stringed harp.

3Sing to Him a new song;
play skillfully, with shouts of joy.

4For the word of the LORD is upright,
and all His work is done in faithfulness.

5He loves righteousness and justice;
the earth is full of the loyal love of the LORD.

6By the word of the LORD the heavens were made,
and by the breath of His mouth all their host.

7He gathers the waters of the sea as a heap;
He puts the deeps in storehouses.

8Let all the earth fear the LORD;
let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of Him.

9For He spoke, and it came to be;
He commanded, and it stood firm.

10The LORD brings the counsel of the nations to nothing;
He frustrates the plans of the peoples.

11The counsel of the LORD stands forever,
the plans of His heart to all generations.

12Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD,
the people He has chosen as His inheritance.

13The LORD looks down from heaven;
He sees all the children of man;

14from the place where He sits enthroned He looks out
on all the inhabitants of the earth,

15He who forms the hearts of them all
and understands all their deeds.

16The king is not saved by his great army;
a warrior is not rescued by his great strength.

17The horse is a false hope for victory,
and by its great might it cannot rescue.

18The eye of the LORD is on those who fear Him,
on those who hope in His loyal love,

19to deliver their soul from death
and keep them alive in famine.

20Our soul waits for the LORD;
He is our help and our shield.

21For our heart is glad in Him,
because we trust in His holy name.

22Let Your loyal love, LORD, be upon us,
even as we hope in You.

Notes

  • The psalm — one of the few psalms in the first book of the Psalter without a title; it has twenty-two verses, the number of the letters of the Hebrew alphabet, though it is not an acrostic. It takes up the last words of Psalm 32, shout for joy… you upright.

  • v3 "a new song" — a song for a new act of God (40:3; 96:1; Isaiah 42:10; Revelation 5:9).

  • v6 "By the word of the LORD the heavens were made" — And God said… and it was so (Genesis 1:6–9). The breath of His mouth is ruach piv: the Church Fathers read the verse of the Word and the Spirit together at creation (Genesis 1:2; John 1:1–3).

  • v7 "He gathers the waters of the sea as a heap" — ka-ned, as at the crossing of the sea (Exodus 15:8; Joshua 3:13). The Greek reads nod, as in a wineskin.

  • v9 "He spoke, and it came to be" — hu amar va-yehi, the creative word of Genesis 1.

  • v12 "Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD" — Israel chosen as God's inheritance (Deuteronomy 32:9; Exodus 19:5–6).

  • vv13–15 "He who forms the hearts of them all" — ha-yotser, the potter (Genesis 2:7): the Maker of hearts understands what they do.

  • vv16–17 "The horse is a false hope" — as in 20:7: armies and horses do not save (Hosea 1:7).

  • v18 "The eye of the LORD is on those who fear Him" — against the eye He casts on all mankind (v13): He watches over His own (34:15).

chapters.title: Taste and See
chapters.html:
Psalms 34

Of David, when he changed his behavior before Abimelech, who drove him out, and he went away.

1I will bless the LORD at all times;
His praise will always be in my mouth.

2My soul makes its boast in the LORD;
let the humble hear and be glad.

3Magnify the LORD with me,
and let us exalt His name together.

4I sought the LORD, and He answered me
and delivered me from all my fears.

5Those who look to Him are radiant,
and their faces will never be ashamed.

6This poor man cried, and the LORD heard
and saved him out of all his troubles.

7The messenger of the LORD camps
around those who fear Him, and rescues them.

8Taste and see that the LORD is good;
blessed is the man who takes refuge in Him.

9Fear the LORD, you His holy ones,
for those who fear Him lack nothing.

10The young lions suffer want and hunger,
but those who seek the LORD lack no good thing.

11Come, children, listen to me;
I will teach you the fear of the LORD.

12Who is the man who desires life
and loves many days, to see good?

13Keep your tongue from evil
and your lips from speaking deceit.

14Turn away from evil and do good;
seek peace and pursue it.

15The eyes of the LORD are toward the righteous,
and His ears toward their cry.

16The face of the LORD is against those who do evil,
to cut off the memory of them from the earth.

17They cry, and the LORD hears
and delivers them out of all their troubles.

18The LORD is near to the brokenhearted
and saves the crushed in spirit.

19Many are the troubles of the righteous,
but the LORD delivers him out of them all.

20He keeps all his bones;
not one of them is broken.

21Evil will kill the wicked,
and those who hate the righteous will be held guilty.

22The LORD redeems the soul of His servants;
none who take refuge in Him will be held guilty.

Notes

  • The title "when he changed his behavior before Abimelech" — David's feigned madness before the king of Gath, called Achish in 1 Samuel 21:10–15. Abimelech, my father is king, may have been a royal title of the Philistine kings (Genesis 20:2; 26:1).

  • The psalm — an acrostic, each verse beginning with the next letter of the alphabet (one letter is missing); the last verse stands outside the alphabet, as in Psalm 25.

  • v5 "Those who look to Him are radiant" — naharu, beam with light, as Moses' face shone (Exodus 34:29; Isaiah 60:5).

  • v6 "This poor man" — David speaking of himself.

  • v7 "The messenger of the LORD" — mal'akh YHWH, messenger, as the word table has it; the one who camped around Jacob at Mahanaim, the camp of God (Genesis 32:1–2; 2 Kings 6:17).

  • v8 "Taste and see that the LORD is good" — ta'amu, the word used in the title for David's behavior (ta'mo, his sense): he feigned a lack of sense, and here invites others to taste. If indeed you have tasted that the Lord is good (1 Peter 2:3).

  • vv12–16 — quoted in full by Peter (1 Peter 3:10–12).

  • v18 "the brokenhearted… the crushed in spirit" — A broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise (51:17; Isaiah 57:15).

  • v20 "not one of them is broken" — quoted by John of Jesus on the cross, whose legs were not broken (John 19:36), with the law of the Passover lamb (Exodus 12:46).

chapters.title: Contend, LORD, with Those Who Contend with Me
chapters.html:
Psalms 35

Of David.

1Contend, LORD, with those who contend with me;
fight against those who fight against me.

2Take hold of shield and buckler
and rise up to help me.

3Draw out the spear and close the way against those who pursue me;
say to my soul, "I am your salvation."

4Let them be put to shame and disgraced
who seek my life;
let them be turned back and confounded
who devise evil against me.

5Let them be like chaff before the wind,
with the messenger of the LORD driving them on.

6Let their way be dark and slippery,
with the messenger of the LORD pursuing them.

7For without cause they hid their net for me;
without cause they dug a pit for my soul.

8Let ruin come on him when he does not know it,
and let the net he hid catch him;
let him fall into it, to his ruin.

9My soul will rejoice in the LORD,
exulting in His salvation.

10All my bones will say,
"LORD, who is like You,
who rescues the poor from one too strong for him,
the poor and needy from the one who robs him?"

11Violent witnesses rise up;
they ask me of things I do not know.

12They repay me evil for good;
my soul is bereaved.

13But I, when they were sick, was clothed in sackcloth;
I afflicted my soul with fasting,
and my prayer returned to my own bosom.

14I went about as for my friend or my brother;
as one who mourns for his mother, I bowed down in mourning.

15But at my stumbling they rejoiced and gathered;
they gathered against me, the lame I did not know;
they tore at me and did not stop.

16Like godless mockers at a feast,
they gnash their teeth at me.

17Lord, how long will You look on?
Bring back my soul from their ruin,
my only life from the young lions.

18I will give You thanks in the great congregation;
among a mighty people I will praise You.

19Let not those who are my enemies without reason rejoice over me,
nor those who hate me without cause wink the eye.

20For they do not speak peace,
but against the quiet ones of the land
they devise words of deceit.

21They open their mouths wide against me;
they say, "Aha, aha! Our eyes have seen it!"

22You have seen, LORD; do not keep silent!
Lord, do not be far from me!

23Wake up and rouse Yourself for my right,
my God and my Lord, for my cause!

24Vindicate me, LORD my God, according to Your righteousness,
and let them not rejoice over me.

25Let them not say in their hearts, "Aha, our desire!"
Let them not say, "We have swallowed him up."

26Let them be put to shame and confounded together
who rejoice at my trouble;
let them be clothed with shame and disgrace
who make themselves great against me.

27Let those who delight in my righteousness shout for joy and be glad,
and say always, "Great is the LORD,
who delights in the peace of His servant!"

28Then my tongue will tell of Your righteousness,
of Your praise all the day long.

  • vv1–3 "Contend… fight… Take hold of shield and buckler" — God called on as advocate in court (contend, riv) and as warrior in battle. Close the way is segor, which some take as battle-axe.

  • vv5–6 "the messenger of the LORD" — mal'akh YHWH, as in 34:7, now driving the enemy before him.

  • v7 "without cause" — chinnam, twice, the word of Job 1:9 and 2:3; again in v19.

  • v13 "my prayer returned to my own bosom" — either bowed down in prayer, head to the chest (1 Kings 18:42), or the prayer for them came back unanswered on the one who prayed it (Matthew 10:13).

  • v15 "the lame I did not know" — nekhim, smitten ones, perhaps cripples (2 Samuel 4:4); the word is uncertain, and some read nokhrim, strangers.

  • v16 "Like godless mockers at a feast" — lo'agei ma'og, mockers for a cake, men who mock for a meal; the line is hard.

  • v19 "those who hate me without cause" — sone'ai chinnam, quoted by Jesus of Himself: They hated Me without a cause (John 15:25; 69:4).

  • v20 "the quiet ones of the land" — rig'ei erets, the peaceful, who make no trouble.

  • v23 "my God and my Lord" — Elohai va-Adonai; Thomas's confession of the risen Jesus, My Lord and my God (John 20:28).

  • v27 "who delights in the peace of His servant" — shelom avdo, the servant's well-being, his shalom.

chapters.title: In Your Light We See Light
chapters.html:
Psalms 36

For the director. Of the servant of the LORD, of David.

1Transgression speaks to the wicked
deep within my heart;
there is no fear of God
before his eyes.

2For he flatters himself in his own eyes
that his iniquity will not be found out and hated.

3The words of his mouth are trouble and deceit;
he has stopped acting wisely and doing good.

4He plots trouble on his bed;
he sets himself on a way that is not good;
he does not reject evil.

5LORD, Your loyal love is in the heavens,
Your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.

6Your righteousness is like the mountains of God;
Your judgments are a great deep;
man and beast You save, LORD.

7How precious is Your loyal love, God!
The children of man take refuge in the shadow of Your wings.

8They are filled with the abundance of Your house,
and You give them drink from the river of Your delights.

9For with You is the fountain of life;
in Your light we see light.

10Continue Your loyal love to those who know You,
and Your righteousness to the upright in heart.

11Let not the foot of pride come against me,
nor the hand of the wicked drive me away.

12There the doers of iniquity have fallen;
they are thrust down and cannot rise.

Notes

  • The title "Of the servant of the LORD" — as in Psalm 18; David as the servant of God (2 Samuel 7:5).

  • v1 "Transgression speaks to the wicked deep within my heart" — ne'um pesha, an oracle of transgression: sin speaks to the wicked man as God speaks to a prophet. The Hebrew has my heart, as though the psalmist hears it; the Greek, Syriac and some Hebrew manuscripts read his heart.

  • v1 "there is no fear of God before his eyes" — the last line of Paul's charge against all mankind (Romans 3:18).

  • v4 "He plots trouble on his bed" — the opposite of the righteous man who meditates at night (4:4; 63:6; Micah 2:1).

  • vv5–6 — God's chesed, faithfulness, righteousness and judgments, as high as the heavens, as great as the mountains and the deep: the whole world measured against the wicked man's small plotting.

  • v6 "man and beast You save" — God's care reaches to the animals (104:14–15; Jonah 4:11).

  • v7 "the shadow of Your wings" — as in 17:8.

  • v8 "the river of Your delights" — adanekha, Your Edens, the word of the garden of Eden, which was watered by a river (Genesis 2:10; Ezekiel 47:1–12).

  • v9 "in Your light we see light" — the Church has read it of the Son, light from light, the true light that gives light to everyone (John 1:4–9).

  • v12 "There the doers of iniquity have fallen" — there, at the place and time of God's judgment, seen by the psalmist as already done.

chapters.title: Do Not Fret Because of Evildoers
chapters.html:
Psalms 37

Of David.

1Do not fret because of evildoers;
do not envy those who do wrong.

2For they will soon wither like the grass
and fade like the green plant.

3Trust in the LORD and do good;
dwell in the land and feed on faithfulness.

4Delight yourself in the LORD,
and He will give you the desires of your heart.

5Commit your way to the LORD;
trust in Him, and He will act.

6He will bring out your righteousness like the light,
and your justice like the noonday.

7Be still before the LORD and wait patiently for Him;
do not fret because of the one who prospers in his way,
because of the man who carries out his schemes.

8Refrain from anger and forsake wrath;
do not fret; it leads only to evil.

9For evildoers will be cut off,
but those who wait for the LORD will inherit the land.

10In a little while the wicked will be no more;
you will look carefully at his place, and he will not be there.

11But the humble will inherit the land
and delight themselves in abundant peace.

12The wicked plots against the righteous
and gnashes his teeth at him,

13but the Lord laughs at him,
for He sees that his day is coming.

14The wicked have drawn the sword and bent their bow
to bring down the poor and needy,
to slaughter those whose way is upright;

15their sword will enter their own heart,
and their bows will be broken.

16Better is the little that the righteous has
than the abundance of many wicked.

17For the arms of the wicked will be broken,
but the LORD upholds the righteous.

18The LORD knows the days of the blameless,
and their inheritance will last forever;

19they will not be put to shame in an evil time;
in days of famine they will be satisfied.

20But the wicked will perish;
the enemies of the LORD are like the glory of the pastures;
they vanish; like smoke they vanish away.

21The wicked borrows and does not repay,
but the righteous is gracious and gives;

22for those He blesses will inherit the land,
but those He curses will be cut off.

23The steps of a man are established by the LORD,
when He delights in his way;

24though he falls, he will not be cast down,
for the LORD holds his hand.

25I have been young, and now I am old,
yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken
or his children begging for bread.

26All day long he is gracious and lends,
and his children become a blessing.

27Turn away from evil and do good,
and you will dwell forever.

28For the LORD loves justice
and will not forsake His faithful ones.
They are kept forever,
but the children of the wicked will be cut off.

29The righteous will inherit the land
and dwell on it forever.

30The mouth of the righteous utters wisdom,
and his tongue speaks justice.

31The law of his God is in his heart;
his steps do not slip.

32The wicked watches for the righteous
and seeks to put him to death.

33The LORD will not leave him in his hand
or let him be condemned when he is judged.

34Wait for the LORD and keep His way,
and He will lift you up to inherit the land;
you will look on when the wicked are cut off.

35I have seen a wicked man, ruthless,
spreading himself like a green tree in its native soil.

36He passed away, and he was gone;
I sought him, and he could not be found.

37Watch the blameless and see the upright,
for there is a future for the man of peace.

38But transgressors will be destroyed together;
the future of the wicked will be cut off.

39The salvation of the righteous is from the LORD;
He is their stronghold in the time of trouble.

40The LORD helps them and rescues them;
He rescues them from the wicked and saves them,
because they take refuge in Him.

Notes

  • The psalm — an acrostic in pairs of verses, each pair beginning with the next letter of the alphabet: a wisdom psalm, like Proverbs, teaching patience while the wicked prosper (73).

  • v1 "Do not fret" — al titchar, do not get heated, three times (vv1, 7, 8): Fret not yourself because of evildoers (Proverbs 24:19).

  • v3 "feed on faithfulness" — re'eh emunah, or shepherd faithfulness, keep it as a flock.

  • v5 "Commit your way to the LORD" — gol, roll your way onto Him (22:8; Proverbs 16:3).

  • vv9, 11, 22, 29, 34 "inherit the land" — five times, the promise to Abraham's children; v11 is the beatitude, Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth (Matthew 5:5).

  • v13 "the Lord laughs at him" — as in 2:4.

  • v20 "like the glory of the pastures" — ki-yqar karim, the brief splendor of spring grass; the same words can mean like the fat of lambs, burned on the altar and gone up in smoke.

  • v25 "I have been young, and now I am old" — the testimony of a long life; the psalmist speaks from what he has seen, as the wise do (Job 4:7).

  • v31 "The law of his God is in his heart" — I will put My law within them (Jeremiah 31:33; 40:8).

  • v35 "like a green tree in its native soil" — ke-ezrach ra'anan, a tree rooted where it grew, flourishing; it passed away all the same (vv35–36).

chapters.title: Do Not Forsake Me, LORD
chapters.html:
Psalms 38

A psalm of David, to bring to remembrance.

1LORD, do not rebuke me in Your wrath,
nor discipline me in Your fury.

2For Your arrows have sunk into me,
and Your hand has come down on me.

3There is no soundness in my flesh because of Your indignation;
there is no peace in my bones because of my sin.

4For my iniquities have gone over my head;
like a heavy burden, they are too heavy for me.

5My wounds stink and fester
because of my folly.

6I am bent and bowed down greatly;
all the day I go about mourning.

7For my loins are filled with burning,
and there is no soundness in my flesh.

8I am numb and greatly crushed;
I groan because of the turmoil of my heart.

9Lord, all my longing is before You;
my sighing is not hidden from You.

10My heart throbs; my strength has left me,
and the light of my eyes, even that is gone from me.

11My friends and companions stand aloof from my affliction,
and my neighbors stand far off.

12Those who seek my life lay snares;
those who seek my harm speak of ruin
and plot deceit all day long.

13But I am like a deaf man; I do not hear,
like a mute who does not open his mouth.

14I have become like a man who does not hear,
in whose mouth are no rebukes.

15For in You, LORD, I hope;
You will answer, Lord my God.

16For I said, "Let them not rejoice over me,
who make themselves great against me when my foot slips."

17For I am ready to fall,
and my pain is always before me.

18I confess my iniquity;
I am troubled because of my sin.

19My enemies are alive and strong,
and many are those who hate me without reason.

20Those who repay evil for good
accuse me because I follow what is good.

21Do not forsake me, LORD;
my God, do not be far from me.

22Hurry to help me,
Lord, my salvation.

Notes

  • The title "to bring to remembrance" — le-hazkir, also over Psalm 70; perhaps to bring the sufferer to God's remembrance, or a term of the memorial offering (Leviticus 2:2).

  • The psalm — the third of the penitential psalms (see 6). It opens with the words of 6:1.

  • v2 "Your arrows have sunk into me" — God the archer, as in Job 6:4 and 16:12–13.

  • vv3–8 — sickness of body felt as the weight of sin: soundness (metom), peace (shalom), wounds that stink, burning in the loins. The psalmist does not say all sickness comes from sin; he says his has.

  • v11 "my affliction" — nig'i, my stroke, the word for a mark of disease (Leviticus 13:2–3); the friends keep their distance as from a man with blight.

  • vv13–14 "like a deaf man… like a mute" — he does not answer his accusers; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter… He opened not His mouth (Isaiah 53:7).

  • v19 "My enemies are alive and strong" — chayyim, living; perhaps a slip for chinnam, without cause, which would match without reason in the next line (35:19; 69:4).

  • v20 "because I follow what is good" — the read form, rodfi; the written form has the same word spelled with an extra letter.

chapters.title: A Guest with You
chapters.html:
Psalms 39

For the director: for Jeduthun. A psalm of David.

1I said, "I will guard my ways,
so that I do not sin with my tongue;
I will keep a muzzle on my mouth
while the wicked are in front of me."

2I was mute and silent;
I held my peace, to no good,
and my pain was stirred up.

3My heart grew hot within me;
as I mused, the fire burned;
then I spoke with my tongue:

4"LORD, make me know my end,
and what is the measure of my days;
let me know how fleeting I am.

5You have made my days a few handbreadths,
and my lifetime is as nothing before You.
Surely every man, even standing firm, is only a breath. Selah

6Surely a man walks about as a shadow;
surely for a breath they are in turmoil;
he heaps up, and does not know who will gather.

7Now, Lord, what do I wait for?
My hope is in You.

8Rescue me from all my transgressions;
do not make me the scorn of the fool.

9I am mute; I do not open my mouth,
for You are the one who has done it.

10Take away Your stroke from me;
I am worn out by the blows of Your hand.

11With rebukes for iniquity You discipline a man;
You consume like a moth what he holds dear;
surely every man is a breath. Selah

12Hear my prayer, LORD,
and listen to my cry;
do not be silent at my tears.
For I am a guest with You,
a resident, like all my fathers.

13Look away from me, that I may smile again,
before I go and am no more."

Notes

  • The title "for Jeduthun" — one of David's chief musicians, with Asaph and Heman (1 Chronicles 16:41–42; 25:1); also over Psalms 62 and 77.

  • vv1–3 — the psalmist resolves to keep silent before the wicked, as in 38:13, but the fire in his heart breaks out in prayer, not complaint (Jeremiah 20:9).

  • v4 "make me know my end" — Teach us to number our days (90:12).

  • v5 "a few handbreadths" — tefachot, the width of a hand, the smallest measure. A breath is hevel, three times in the psalm (vv5, 6, 11), the word of Ecclesiastes.

  • v6 "a man walks about as a shadow" — be-tselem, as an image, a phantom (73:20; Job 8:9).

  • v6 "he heaps up, and does not know who will gather" — Fool! This night your soul is required of you, and the things you have prepared, whose will they be? (Luke 12:20).

  • v9 "for You are the one who has done it" — the psalmist accepts his trouble from God's hand, as Job did (Job 2:10).

  • v11 "You consume like a moth what he holds dear" — the moth that eats a garment slowly (Job 13:28; Isaiah 50:9).

  • v12 "a guest with You, a resident" — ger and toshav, as the word table has them: the land is Mine; for you are guests and residents with Me (Leviticus 25:23; 1 Chronicles 29:15; Hebrews 11:13).

  • v13 "Look away from me" — hasha, gaze away: the plea of Job 7:19 and 10:20, Leave me alone, that I may have a little cheer.

chapters.title: I Delight to Do Your Will
chapters.html:
Psalms 40

For the director. Of David. A psalm.

1I waited patiently for the LORD;
He inclined to me and heard my cry.

2He drew me up from the pit of ruin,
out of the miry clay,
and set my feet on a rock,
making my steps secure.

3He put a new song in my mouth,
a song of praise to our God.
Many will see and fear,
and will trust in the LORD.

4Blessed is the man who makes the LORD his trust,
who does not turn to the proud,
to those who go astray after falsehood.

5You have done many things, LORD my God,
Your wonders and Your thoughts toward us;
none can compare with You.
If I would declare and speak of them,
they are more than can be counted.

6Sacrifice and offering You did not desire;
ears You have dug for me;
burnt offering and sin offering You did not ask for.

7Then I said, "Here I have come;
in the scroll of the book it is written of me.

8I delight to do Your will, my God;
Your law is within my inmost being."

9I have told the good news of righteousness in the great congregation;
I have not held back my lips,
as You know, LORD.

10I have not hidden Your righteousness within my heart;
I have spoken of Your faithfulness and Your salvation;
I have not concealed Your loyal love and Your truth
from the great congregation.

11As for You, LORD, do not hold back Your compassion from me;
let Your loyal love and Your truth always keep me.

12For evils without number have surrounded me;
my iniquities have overtaken me, and I cannot see;
they are more than the hairs of my head,
and my heart has failed me.

13Be pleased, LORD, to rescue me;
LORD, hurry to help me.

14Let them be put to shame and confounded together
who seek my life to sweep it away;
let them be turned back and disgraced
who delight in my harm.

15Let them be appalled because of their shame
who say to me, "Aha, aha!"

16But let all who seek You
rejoice and be glad in You;
let those who love Your salvation
say always, "Great is the LORD!"

17As for me, I am poor and needy,
but the Lord thinks of me.
You are my help and my deliverer;
my God, do not delay.

Notes

  • v2 "the pit of ruin… the miry clay" — bor sha'on, the pit of roaring, of tumult, and tit ha-yaven, the mud of a cistern, like the one Jeremiah sank into (Jeremiah 38:6).

  • v3 "a new song" — as in 33:3.

  • v6 "ears You have dug for me" — oznayim karita li: God has opened the psalmist's ears to hear and obey, which He wants more than sacrifice (1 Samuel 15:22; Isaiah 50:5). The Greek reads a body You have prepared for me, and Hebrews 10:5–7 quotes the Greek of vv6–8 as the words of Christ coming into the world.

  • v7 "Here I have come; in the scroll of the book it is written of me" — the obedient servant presents himself; the scroll may be the law that the king was to copy and keep (Deuteronomy 17:18–19).

  • v8 "Your law is within my inmost being" — be-tokh me'ai, in my inward parts: the law written on the heart (37:31; Jeremiah 31:33).

  • v9 "I have told the good news" — bissarti, the verb of good tidings (Isaiah 40:9; 52:7), the root of the Greek gospel in later use.

  • v12 "evils without number" — ra'ot, troubles, and his own iniquities with them: the thanksgiving of vv1–10 turns to a new plea.

  • vv13–17 — repeated, with small differences, as Psalm 70.

  • v17 "the Lord thinks of me" — Adonai yachashov li; Psalm 70:5 has God, hurry to me.

speech.text: Psalms 40
I waited patiently for the LORD; He inclined to me and heard my cry.
He drew me up from the pit of ruin, out of the miry clay, and set my feet on a rock, making my steps secure.
He put a new song in my mouth, a song of praise to our God. Many will see and fear, and will trust in the LORD.
Blessed is the man who makes the LORD his trust, who does not turn to the proud, to those who go astray after falsehood.
You have done many things, LORD my God, Your wonders and Your thoughts toward us; none can compare with You. If I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be counted.
Sacrifice and offering You did not desire; ears You have dug for me; burnt offering and sin offering You did not ask for.
Then I said, "Here I have come; in the scroll of the book it is written of me.
I delight to do Your will, my God; Your law is within my inmost being."
I have told the good news of righteousness in the great congregation; I have not held back my lips, as You know, LORD.
I have not hidden Your righteousness within my heart; I have spoken of Your faithfulness and Your salvation; I have not concealed Your loyal love and Your truth from the great congregation.
As for You, LORD, do not hold back Your compassion from me; let Your loyal love and Your truth always keep me.
For evils without number have surrounded me; my iniquities have overtaken me, and I cannot see; they are more than the hairs of my head, and my heart has failed me.
Be pleased, LORD, to rescue me; LORD, hurry to help me.
Let them be put to shame and confounded together who seek my life to sweep it away; let them be turned back and disgraced who delight in my harm.
Let them be appalled because of their shame who say to me, "Aha, aha!"
But let all who seek You rejoice and be glad in You; let those who love Your salvation say always, "Great is the LORD!"
As for me, I am poor and needy, but the Lord thinks of me. You are my help and my deliverer; my God, do not delay.

chapters.title: Blessed Is the One Who Considers the Poor
chapters.html:
Psalms 41

For the director. A psalm of David.

1Blessed is the one who considers the poor;
in the day of trouble the LORD delivers him;

2the LORD keeps him and keeps him alive;
he is called blessed in the land;
You do not give him up to the will of his enemies.

3The LORD sustains him on his sickbed;
in his illness You turn over all his bed.

4As for me, I said, "LORD, be gracious to me;
heal my soul, for I have sinned against You."

5My enemies speak evil of me:
"When will he die, and his name perish?"

6If one comes to see me, he speaks emptiness;
his heart gathers trouble for itself;
he goes out and speaks of it.

7All who hate me whisper together against me;
they plot harm against me:

8"A thing of worthlessness is poured into him;
now that he lies down, he will not rise again."

9Even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted,
who ate my bread, has lifted up his heel against me.

10But You, LORD, be gracious to me and raise me up,
so that I may repay them.

11By this I know that You delight in me:
my enemy does not shout in triumph over me.

12As for me, You uphold me in my integrity
and set me before Your face forever.

13Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting.
Amen and Amen.

Notes

  • v1 "Blessed is the one who considers the poor" — maskil el dal, who pays heed to the weak, as God does; the psalm begins and the first book of the Psalms ends with blessed (1:1).

  • v3 "You turn over all his bed" — God as nurse, changing the sick man's bed; or, You change all his lying down, turning sickness to health.

  • v4 "heal my soul, for I have sinned against You" — sickness and sin together, as in 38:3.

  • v8 "A thing of worthlessness" — devar beliyya'al, a deadly disease, or a curse laid on him.

  • v9 "the man of my peace… has lifted up his heel against me" — ish shelomi, a trusted friend, as Ahithophel was to David (2 Samuel 15:12). Jesus quotes the verse of Judas, He who ate My bread has lifted his heel against Me (John 13:18).

  • v10 "so that I may repay them" — the king's right to deal with rebels; the psalmist asks to be raised to do it.

  • v12 "my integrity" — tummi, as in 26:1.

  • v13 "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel… Amen and Amen" — the doxology that closes the first of the five books of the Psalms (1–41); the others end at 72, 89, 106 and 150.

chapters.title: As a Deer Longs for Streams of Water
chapters.html:
Psalms 42

For the director. A Maskil of the sons of Korah.

1As a deer longs for streams of water,
so my soul longs for You, God.

2My soul thirsts for God, for the living God.
When shall I come and appear before God?

3My tears have been my bread day and night,
while they say to me all day long,
"Where is your God?"

4These things I remember as I pour out my soul within me:
how I would pass along with the throng
and lead them in procession to the house of God,
with the sound of shouts of joy and thanksgiving,
a multitude keeping the feast.

5Why are you bowed down, my soul,
and why are you in turmoil within me?
Hope in God, for I will yet praise Him
for the salvation of His presence.

6My God, my soul is bowed down within me;
therefore I remember You
from the land of the Jordan and the Hermons,
from Mount Mizar.

7Deep calls to deep
at the roar of Your waterfalls;
all Your breakers and Your waves
have gone over me.

8By day the LORD commands His loyal love,
and at night His song is with me,
a prayer to the God of my life.

9I will say to God my rock,
"Why have You forgotten me?
Why do I go about mourning
because of the oppression of the enemy?"

10As with a shattering in my bones, my adversaries taunt me,
while they say to me all day long,
"Where is your God?"

11Why are you bowed down, my soul,
and why are you in turmoil within me?
Hope in God, for I will yet praise Him,
the salvation of my face and my God.

Notes

  • v1 and the second book of the Psalms (42–72) — in these psalms God is mostly called Elohim, God, where the first book has YHWH, the LORD.

  • The title "of the sons of Korah" — the Levite singers descended from Korah (Numbers 26:11; 1 Chronicles 6:31–37), named over Psalms 42–49, 84–85 and 87–88.

  • v5 and Psalm 43 — Psalms 42 and 43 are one poem in three parts, with the same refrain (42:5, 11; 43:5); Psalm 43 has no title, and many Hebrew manuscripts join the two.

  • v2 "When shall I come and appear before God?" — ve-era'eh, be seen, the word for appearing at the temple at the feasts (Exodus 23:17); with other vowels, ve-ereh, and see the face of God.

  • v4 "how I would pass along with the throng" — the pilgrim procession to Jerusalem at the feasts (122:1–4; Isaiah 30:29). The psalmist is now far away.

  • v5 "for the salvation of His presence" — yeshu'ot panav, the salvations of His face; the refrain in v11 and 43:5 has panai ve-Elohai, of my face, and my God. Many Hebrew manuscripts and the Greek read v5 as v11.

  • v6 "the land of the Jordan and the Hermons, from Mount Mizar" — the far north, where the Jordan rises below Mount Hermon; Mizar, little, is not otherwise known.

  • v7 "Deep calls to deep" — the torrents of the Jordan's sources roaring down from Hermon become the waves of trouble passing over him, as over Jonah (Jonah 2:3).

  • v8 "By day the LORD commands His loyal love" — the only use of YHWH in Psalms 42–43.

  • vv3, 10 "Where is your God?" — the taunt of those around him, as at the cross, He trusts in God; let God deliver Him now (Matthew 27:43; Joel 2:17).

chapters.title: Send Out Your Light and Your Truth
chapters.html:
Psalms 43

1Vindicate me, God, and plead my cause
against an unfaithful nation;
from the man of deceit and injustice rescue me.

2For You are the God of my stronghold;
why have You rejected me?
Why do I go about mourning
because of the oppression of the enemy?

3Send out Your light and Your truth; let them lead me;
let them bring me to Your holy mountain
and to Your dwellings.

4Then I will come to the altar of God,
to God, my exceeding joy,
and I will praise You with the lyre,
God, my God.

5Why are you bowed down, my soul,
and why are you in turmoil within me?
Hope in God, for I will yet praise Him,
the salvation of my face and my God.

Notes

  • The psalm — the third part of the poem begun in Psalm 42 (see the note there); it has no title of its own.

  • v1 "an unfaithful nation" — goy lo chasid, a people without chesed, without loyal love.

  • v2 "Why do I go about mourning" — the words of 42:9, with rejected for forgotten.

  • v3 "Send out Your light and Your truth; let them lead me" — light and truth as God's messengers, guides on the road back to the temple (27:1; 57:3).

  • v4 "God, my exceeding joy" — El simchat gili, God, the joy of my rejoicing.

  • v5 — the refrain, as in 42:11, now ending the whole poem in hope.

Send out Your light and Your truth; let them lead me; let them bring me to Your holy mountain and to Your dwellings.
Then I will come to the altar of God, to God, my exceeding joy, and I will praise You with the lyre, God, my God.
Why are you bowed down, my soul, and why are you in turmoil within me? Hope in God, for I will yet praise Him, the salvation of my face and my God.
